Case.description:
One vector: an operation's input and the exact bytes it must produce and
decode from, or (`expect: "reject"`) bytes the operation must refuse. A
rejection's input is only what selects the decoder, if anything. A case
that doesn't say `expect` is exact: `*` picks that when both could hold.
`expect: "accept"` is bytes the operation must read as the input, though
encoding the input needn't give them.

reply.description: The message this end sends, if any. Left out for `finish`.

Compare.description: How a runtime's output must match the bytes: by default, byte for byte.

type.description: When the value's bounds matter; otherwise its own shape is its type

Signed.description: A signed integer as a decimal string.

Type.description:
A type a `decode` case reads into. It covers every shape a generated Rust
type can have. `self` means something only inside a `recursive` type.

Unsigned.description:
An unsigned integer as a decimal string, as 64- and 128-bit integers are
held, so a JSON reader that holds numbers as doubles keeps them exact.

Value.description:
A value as a vector states it: typed, so a runtime knows which width or
shape to encode.
